text:
oncall-bot: ALERT · kvcache growth detected on runtime-prod-gpu-12 · memory trending to OOM, multiple restarts in last 10m (alert=INC-2026-5032) :rotating_light:

maria: taking this. seeing repeated OOM kills on pod runtime-serving-ff12. container restart count 4 in 8m. kicking off quick triage.

maria: `kubectl describe pod runtime-serving-ff12 -n prod` shows OOMKilled, eviction events, paged-attn allocator logs before crash.

maria: logs excerpt: ```[2026-03-17T21:02:14Z] WARN kv_cache: fragment_count=8123, live_pages=1.2M, resident_ratio=0.87
[2026-03-17T21:02:18Z] ERROR runtime::alloc: failed to allocate 128MB -> OOM
[2026-03-17T21:02:19Z] INFO trace: start compaction job id=cmp-73
[2026-03-17T21:02:22Z] FATAL runtime: container panic: CUBLAS_STATUS_EXECUTION_FAILED
```

ajay: noted. can you paste the full CUDA error stack? if drivers mismatch we see execution failures plus memory leak patterns.

maria: full snippet: ```E CUDART: GPU0: cuBLAS err CUBLAS_STATUS_EXECUTION_FAILED at /usr/local/cuda/src/cublas.cu:482
E runtime: cuda driver 11.8, runtime expects 11.7 -> potential incompat.
```

devin: quick mitigations: 1) route traffic off GPU12 to fallback nodes (scale up cpu-backed replicas / route to lower-capacity model variant), 2) trigger kvcache compaction job across nodes, 3) force eviction of stale prefixes via admin API.

sofia: who's impacted? Rachel, can you check customer routing logs / who saw elevated latency or 5xx?

rachel: checking observability — two high-volume customers had 5–10% failed requests in last 12m: cust-acme and cust-lumina. support ticket opened (#SUP-1228) and notified. No data loss reported, only elevated latency and failed generations.

maria: mitigation step 1: bumped eviction threshold on runtime-prod-gpu-12 from 0.75 -> 0.6 to force earlier evictions. Issued compaction `POST /admin/compaction?job=immediate` on the pod.

maria: mitigation step 2: drained node gpu-12 from serving set (mark as maintenance) and routed new requests to gpu-8/gpu-9. traffic shift in progress.

devin: I pushed an emergency rollout to use the smaller kv-window model variant (quantized) for the canary pool to reduce KV usage. Fallback policy applied in routing.

ajay: driver mismatch flagged — majority of affected pods on that node are on container image rt:v2026.03.12 which expects cuda-11.7. Node shows driver 11.8. Rolling driver downgrade not ideal; prefer restart nodes with pinned runtime image that tolerates 11.8. I'll coordinate infra.

sofia: customer comms draft approved: short note, impact summary, ETA for mitigation. Support to send to affected customers in 15m.

maria: after compaction, mem sampling shows resident dropped ~18%, allocator fragmentation still nontrivial. We're seeing slow refill when workload resumes.

maria: observed pattern looks like paged-attn allocator fragmentation + incremental KV cache growth (sticky entries). Possible slow leak on cache insertion path under rare race.

devin: long term action items (quick list): add periodic compaction cron, add admin API endpoint to sweep KV by prefix age, add leak-detection metric (insertion rate vs resident growth), and add unit/regression test for kvcache hotpath.

ajay: immediate infra action: quarantine gpu-12, schedule node reprovision to use runtime build rt:v2026.03.15 which includes allocator fix from last week. Will coordinate with infra to avoid rolling all nodes.

maria: creating incident runbook note: linking logs, heap profiles, kv-allocator counters, and compaction traces. tagging for full postmortem.

sofia: severity update: downgraded to Sev2 -> customers impacted but mitigation in progress and routing stabilized. Will keep monitoring for 2h.

rachel: support updated customers and added temporary rate-limits for affected tenants to avoid retries amplifying allocator pressure.

maria: next steps: capture heap profile from one affected pod before it gets reprovisioned (`gcore` + /proc/pid/maps), preserve kernel coredumps, and upload to S3 path `s3://redwood-incidents/INC-2026-5032/`.

devin: noted. I'm adding a canary that runs high-prefix-churn workload in staging against rt:v2026.03.15 to validate compaction behavior.

ajay: follow-ups for postmortem: 1) add alert for sustained resident_ratio > 0.8 for 10m, 2) add automated compaction when resident growth rate > X MB/min, 3) coordinate driver/runtime compatibility matrix in infra runbook.

sofia: thanks team. reopening channel if node reprovision or customer impact changes. I'll synthesize timeline and assign owners for follow-up items. :white_check_mark:

maria: leaving handoff to ajay for infra, devin for runtime fix, and rachel for support follow-ups. ping me if canary shows regression. :thumbsup:
